over.intro: I’m Afonso, a student in Ghent. I like working with typography, image and colour, and I pay attention to detail.
over.p1: I started with STEM techniques, then studied Graphic Techniques, and now I study Crossmedia at Don Bosco Sint-Denijs-Westrem. In my school projects I make posters, editorial layouts, visual identities, small websites, photos and films.
over.p2: I want to understand why a design works, and I keep refining my approach through school projects and personal work. Outside school I play sports, like to travel and follow technology.
over.p3: I’m looking for a place where I can learn, take feedback on board and contribute to real projects.
over.software_lijst: Photoshop, Illustrator, InDesign, Premiere Pro, After Effects, Lightroom, Figma, HTML/CSS
privacy.beschrijving: Privacy and rights on the website of Afonso Matos da Cruz.
privacy.k2: What data does this website collect?
privacy.t1: Afonso Matos da Cruz, Ghent, Belgium. Contact: afonsomatos820@gmail.com.
privacy.t2: None automatically. The website uses no cookies, no analytics or tracking services and stores nothing in your browser. That is why there is no cookie banner. The hosting provider may keep technical log files, such as your IP address and the time of your visit; this is needed to run the site and keep it secure.
privacy.t3: If you fill in the form, your name, email address, subject and message are sent to my email address via the service Formspree, which acts as an external processor. I only use your details to reply and do not keep them longer than necessary. The same applies if you email me directly.
privacy.t4: The typeface Inter Tight is loaded from this website itself; there is no connection to Google Fonts. Instagram and YouTube are plain links: only when you click them do you reach their websites, where their privacy rules apply.
privacy.t5: You can ask which data I hold about you, have it corrected or erased, or object to its use. Email me for this. You can also lodge a complaint with the Belgian Data Protection Authority (gegevensbeschermingsautoriteit.be).
privacy.t6: I made the designs, photos, films and texts on this website as a school assignment or personal project. You may not copy or reuse them without my permission. Some designs use other people’s imagery, such as photos or artworks, as part of a school assignment; the rights to that material remain with their owners. If you want something changed or removed, email me. The typeface Inter Tight is licensed under the SIL Open Font License; the licence text is in the lettertypen folder.
privacy.titel: Privacy and rights — Afonso Matos da Cruz
project.disco.beschrijving: School project Disco Revisited by Afonso Matos da Cruz: moodboards, an editorial spread, a motion design video and two websites about disco and the Memphis movement.
project.disco.gemaakt: Moodboards, editorial spread, motion design and two websites
project.disco.intro: A project about disco as visual culture: big typography, mirror balls, colour and rhythm. Starting from the film Saturday Night Fever (1977), I developed an editorial spread, a short motion design video and two websites, one of them about the Memphis group.
project.disco.moodboards.tekst: The project started with image: two moodboards collecting colours, shapes and atmosphere from which everything else was built.
project.disco.spread.tekst: A double page with the title ‘DISCO’ in outline letters, a yellow-orange subtitle ‘Ritme, licht en vrijheid’, a violet field with a quote and a cut-out mirror-ball figure in the middle. The text runs in columns and boxes around the images: from underground to mainstream, the sound, image and style, and the 12-inch single.
project.disco.video.tekst: A short motion design video inspired by Saturday Night Fever. The video is also shown under Film.
project.disco.website1.tekst: The spread translated to the web: a dark page with yellow subheadings, the video and a box about the 12-inch single. Built with HTML and CSS, shown here as a screenshot.
project.disco.website2.tekst: A second site about the Memphis movement, which began in Italy in 1981 around Ettore Sottsass: bright colours, geometric shapes and patterns. Built with HTML and CSS, shown here as a screenshot.
project.oostende.beschrijving: School project Seaside Bathing Culture in Ostend by Afonso Matos da Cruz: a visual style guide, an editorial spread, a character with animation and two websites about Ostend.
project.oostende.gemaakt: Style guide, editorial spread, illustration with animation and two websites
project.oostende.intro: A project about the history of bathing culture in Ostend, from the Belle Époque to today. I built a visual identity around it: a style guide with typography and colour, an editorial spread, an illustration with animation and two websites.
project.oostende.ondertitel: From bathing machine to beach club
project.oostende.personage.tekst: A vector illustration of a figure with a black hat and blue apron, with zigzag lines as texture, and a short animation of it. The animation is also shown under Film.
project.oostende.spread.tekst: A double page in the style of the guide: a large title in Bodoni Moda, a bathing machine as a cut-out image, wavy lines and columns about the birth of the seaside resort, elegance on the beach and the evolution of swimwear. At the bottom, a contrast between then and now.
project.oostende.stijlhandleiding.tekst: The foundation of the project, in four parts: typography, colour palette, colour variations and visual identity. Bodoni Moda is used for titles and accents, Lora for running text. The colours come from the coast: Storm Gray, Mist White and Sand Beige as the base, supplemented by Slate Blue, Ochre Gold and Cream Ivory, with Rust Red as a sparing accent.
project.oostende.website1.tekst: A tourist site about Ostend with eight places you should not miss, a section about the city and a contact form. Built with HTML and CSS, shown here as a screenshot.
project.oostende.website2.tekst: A storytelling site in the style of the style guide, with the sections Story, Evolution and Image archive. Built with HTML and CSS, shown here as a screenshot.
project.smak.affiche.tekst: The poster for the 4D/A Graphic Techniques exhibition at the S.M.A.K. The title is set in a serif, with one coloured letter per word; the pixel image carries the page.
project.smak.animatie.tekst: The same poster, now as a short animation. With light and shadows moving subtly, the graphic construction gets a rhythm of its own on screen.
project.smak.archiefdoos.tekst: An archive box is more than packaging: it says something about the history inside it. I designed the box and its label with attention to layout and typography, so the object fits the context of a historic city archive.
project.smak.archieffoto.tekst: Images are often constructed. I edited an old photo from Ghent in Photoshop by adding contemporary elements. The technique changes what the photo means: what looked like archive becomes a new image.
project.smak.beschrijving: School project Image, Doubt & Construction by Afonso Matos da Cruz: poster, animation, archive box, stop-motion, pixel image, invitation and website around an exhibition at the S.M.A.K. in Ghent.
project.smak.bomen.tekst: Inspired by the photographic work of Marc De Blieck, I looked for structures on the border between recording and composing. The bare trees seem caught by chance, but every element is a choice: viewpoint, format, moment and what falls just outside the frame. Black and white strengthens the graphic character of the branches.
project.smak.gemaakt: Poster, animation, archive box, photo editing, stop-motion, photography, algorithmic image, invitation and website
project.smak.intro: A series of assignments for an exhibition at the S.M.A.K. in Ghent, in which students entered into dialogue with the work of photographer Marc De Blieck. One question keeps returning: do you photograph what is there, or do you construct what the viewer sees? I explored it through a poster, animation, an object, stop-motion, an algorithmic image, print and a website.
project.smak.ondertitel: A series of assignments around an exhibition at the S.M.A.K.
project.smak.pixelbeeld.tekst: This image did not start from a sketch, but from numbers. An online pixel tool generated a grid from a base colour; in Illustrator I took colour swatches from the pattern and combined them with a generated circle structure. Then the designing began: moving circles, scaling shapes, leaving emptiness in place. The algorithm supplied the material, I made the composition. The square image measures 15×15 cm, on a portrait format of 20×32 cm set by the Golden Ratio.
project.smak.schaduwaffiche.tekst: How do you tell a story with only light and dark? Starting from Plato’s cave, I designed a poster for an exhibition at the S.M.A.K. that plays with what you can and cannot see. A lantern casts its shadow on the wall; the title ‘Umbra’ and the line ‘Light only shows him the way’ run along the diagonal of the image.
project.smak.schimmenfilm.tekst: A short film in stop-motion and shadow play about social media and identity: the translation of reality into a constructed image.
project.smak.schimmenfilm.titel: The Real Behind The Perfect Picture
project.smak.uitnodiging.tekst: The final step: translating the pixel structures into a tangible product. The front repeats the title and image; the back invites guests to the exhibition and to the reception on Saturday 2 May at 3 p.m.
project.smak.website.tekst: All assignments of the project on one long page, each with a heading, a short explanation and its image. Built with HTML and CSS and shown here as a screenshot.
